name: Google Armstrong County data center campus (Crusoe Goodnight)
summary: AI data center campus near Claude, Armstrong County, in the Texas Panhandle, being developed by Crusoe on about 1,300 acres beside the Goodnight wind farms. Google named Armstrong County as a new campus site in its November 2025 Texas program ($40 billion statewide through 2027), and Crusoe confirmed Google as the end user in September 2026. County tax abatement materials described a first phase of four buildings drawing up to 530 MW, within a two-phase 1,030 MW design. State filings in 2026 added two buildings of about 805,000 sq ft each, together estimated at $1 billion. Amended filings added gas turbines and battery storage, and one report says Crusoe agreed to sell the project to Google.

power_sources.description: Linked to the adjacent Goodnight wind farms: Goodnight 1 (265.5 MW, operating) and Goodnight 2 (similar size, under construction), about 531 MW combined; surplus output returns to the grid.

Amended abatement filings added gas turbines; a January 2026 application sought a 933 MW gas plant serving two buildings without a grid tie. It is a proposal, and Google has not agreed to buy its power.
Battery storage was added to the power plan in amended Armstrong County tax abatement filings.
The county judge said the data center would draw from the ERCOT grid, although the county itself is served through the Southwest Power Pool.

notes: Google's $40 billion Texas figure runs through 2027 and covers new campuses in Armstrong and Haskell Counties among other spending; it is not recorded here as a campus investment. Phase and campus MW figures come from tax abatement materials and are not added together. One state filing gave Building 3 an August 1 completion date (year not stated, presumably 2026) and Building 4 a March 2027 date. New Project Media's article was first published for subscribers; the date used is that of its public posting.
